title: Mój dzień
note: A2 liść at path index 75 · sits directly on a2_sie (74) and a2_chodzic (72). PAYOFF: the first connected paragraph Dad can produce — Codziennie wstaję rano. Myję się. Jem śniadanie. Wychodzę do pracy. Wracam wieczorem. The Zdanie bank is ordered to build to it: single new verb → yes/no question with the same verb → two-sentence pairs → the full five-line day. SIĘ FRAMING is locked to a2_sie: się is a word that BELONGS to the verb, never 'myself'. English helps here for once — 'I wake up', 'I have a wash', 'I get dressed' contain no self either, and the explains say so. Word order in every się sentence is verb + się, the default a2_sie taught; the one exception it allowed (jak + się + verb) does not occur here, and NO clitic-fronting variant (Rano się myję) is offered in accepts, because a2_sie deliberately taught no placement rules. NEW VERBS, 1sg + 2sg only — this is a vocab leaf, not a conjugation unit, so no 3sg/plural anywhere. Each new verb runs on a present class already owned: wstaję/wstajesz and myję się/myjesz się on -ę/-esz (idę, piję); budzę się/budzisz się and wychodzę/wychodzisz on -ę/-isz (chodzę, płacę); ubieram się/ubierasz się on -am/-asz (mieszkam). No new endings in the pack. UNPLANNED ADDITION: jem / jesz. The brief's payoff needs 'Jem śniadanie', but only the infinitive jeść is taught (a1_food) — the present of jeść appears in no teaches_lemmas in the repo and is not in POOL.md. It is taught here as a bare form pair with no class to learn, and śniadanie is neuter so its accusative is identical to the nominative: zero new system. wracać: a1_motion taught only the chunks wracam / wracasz (motion_chunk) and never the infinitive, so wracać alone is new and wracam is recycled untouched. wieczorem is taught as a whole time word next to rano; wieczór is already known and the explain links them without opening the instrumental as a system. FENCED, must not appear: any past form; any 3sg/plural of the new verbs; kłaść się spać and any other new się verb; zwykle, potem, kiedy, o (o siódmej) — all untaught; the habitual partner of any prefixed motion verb; śpię (only the infinitive spać is taught, so bedtime is carried by the known chunk idę spać, and it is fixed to teraz so it never contradicts the codziennie → chodzić rule a2_chodzic just set). NO NEW NOUNS in this pack, therefore no gender badges — every noun in the sentences (śniadanie, obiad, praca, dom, sklep) is recycled and carries its badge in its own pack.

items.explain: budzić się is another verb that travels with się, exactly like uczyć się. The się belongs to the verb — it is not a word for "self", and there is no self in the English either: you simply wake up.
Say it as one unit: myję się. Never try to translate the się on its own.
You have known the dictionary form jeść since the food unit. Its present tense follows no pattern at all — jem, jesz — so learn the two forms as they stand.
You already know the noun wieczór, the evening. wieczorem is the form Polish uses to say when — take it as a single time word and put it in a sentence the way you put rano.

blocks.title: The same verbs · you-form and dictionary form

items.explain: The -ę / -esz endings you already have from idę · idziesz and piję · pijesz.
-ę / -isz, the class of chodzę · chodzisz and płacę · płacisz. The się rides along behind, in both persons.
-am / -asz, the easiest class you own: mieszkam · mieszkasz, nazywam się · nazywasz się. Same endings, plus się.
wracam and wracasz have been in your mouth since the do / z unit. wracać is their dictionary form — the shape you would look up.

sentences.en: Every day I get up in the morning.
sentences.explain: Only the verb is new. wstaję takes the same -ę ending as idę and piję, and codziennie sits exactly where it sat with chodzę.

sentences.en: Do you get up early?
I wake up in the morning.
sentences.explain: budzić się carries its się everywhere, the way uczyć się and czuć się do. The się is part of the verb and stands straight after it — it is not telling you anything about a self.

sentences.en: Do you wake up early?
sentences.explain: czy opens the question and nothing else moves — the się still sits behind its verb, as it did in Czuję się dobrze.

sentences.en: I have a wash in the morning.
sentences.explain: English says I have a wash, not I wash myself, and Polish is the same: myję się is one verb with its own się. Do not look for a word meaning myself in it — there is not one.

sentences.en: Do you have a wash in the morning?
I get dressed at home.
sentences.explain: The endings are the ones from mieszkam and nazywam się — nothing new to learn, only the się to remember.

sentences.en: Do you get dressed in the morning?
I eat breakfast.
sentences.explain: śniadanie is an old word from the food unit, so the only new thing is jem. jeść is one of the few Polish verbs with no ending pattern behind it — jem, jesz, and that is all you need here.

sentences.en: Do you eat breakfast?
I eat lunch at home.
sentences.explain: obiad does not change its shape after jem — it looks exactly as it does in the dictionary. Only feminine nouns like kawa show a different ending as an object.

sentences.en: I go out to work.
sentences.explain: do pracy is the same do + genitive phrase you have used since Idę do pracy. The new verb takes the -ę / -isz endings of chodzę and płacę.

sentences.en: Are you going out to the shop?
I come back in the evening.
sentences.explain: wracam is an old word — the new one is wieczorem. It answers when, just like rano, and it goes in the same slots rano goes in.

sentences.en: I come back from work in the evening.
sentences.explain: Two known halves and one new word: wracam z pracy is the going-home phrase you already own, and wieczorem only says when it happens.

sentences.en: In the evening I'm tired. (m)
sentences.explain: A woman would say Wieczorem jestem zmęczona — the time word never changes, only the adjective does.

sentences.en: Now I'm going to bed.
sentences.explain: Nothing new at all — idę spać is the everyday way to say you are off to bed. teraz is why it is idę and not chodzę: this is happening now, not as a routine.

sentences.en: Every day I get up in the morning. I have a wash.
sentences.explain: Two sentences in a row, and Polish does not need a word for I in either of them — the endings already say who is speaking.

sentences.en: I eat breakfast. I go out to work.
accepts: Jem śniadanie i wychodzę do pracy.
Jem śniadanie i wychodzę do pracy
sentences.explain: You can join the two with i and it stays correct: Jem śniadanie i wychodzę do pracy.

sentences.en: Every day I get up in the morning. I have a wash. I eat breakfast. I go out to work. I come back in the evening.
sentences.pl: Codziennie wstaję rano. Myję się. Jem śniadanie. Wychodzę do pracy. Wracam wieczorem.

Codziennie wstaję rano. Myję się. Jem śniadanie. Wychodzę do pracy. Wieczorem wracam
sentences.explain: This is your whole day in five sentences, and it is the first thing you can say in Polish that runs on past a single line. Say it out loud in order — morning, wash, breakfast, out, back — and the order itself will hold the words for you.
